Chapter 7: The Aftershocks of Trauma
Healing isn’t a straight line, is it? Even after the trial was over, and the headlines had finally faded, those aftershocks of trauma kept rippling through Chanel’s life.
Some days, she felt almost normal. She could laugh with friends, get lost in a good book, even walk through the city without that shadow of fear. But then, there were days when the memories came crashing in—like a wave—leaving her feeling breathless and raw.
Over time, she started to notice the signs. Maybe it was a tightness in her chest, sudden tears, or just this urge to pull away from the world. So, she leaned on little routines—making tea first thing in the morning, sketching quietly in her notebook, or simply calling her sister just to hear her voice. These tiny rituals became her anchors. They reminded her that she was still here... still moving forward, even on the hardest days.
But let’s be real—there were setbacks, too. Sometimes, all it took was a news story, or even a careless comment, to send her spiraling back into that darkness. She fought through insomnia, panic attacks, and that sinking feeling she might never truly be free from what happened. Therapy helped, but it wasn’t easy. It meant digging deep into old wounds, learning how to sit with discomfort, and finding new ways to cope when things felt overwhelming.
Trauma changed her relationships, too. Some friends drifted away, maybe because they didn’t know what to say, or how to help. But others stepped in—offering quiet support, listening without judgment. She learned to let go of the ones who couldn’t walk with her, and to really cherish those who stayed.
Most people never see the invisible scars survivors carry. Chanel became skilled at hiding her pain, putting on a brave face for the world. But deep down, in the privacy of her mind, she battled doubt and fear. Would she ever feel safe again? Could she trust herself—or anyone else—the way she once did?
With time, she discovered something important. Healing wasn’t about erasing the past—it was about learning to live with it. She found strength in being vulnerable, in letting herself feel every emotion, even the hard ones. And she realized it was okay to have bad days, to ask for help, to admit she was still struggling.
The journey was long, and sometimes lonely. But Chanel never gave up. She kept moving forward, one step at a time. Trusting that with patience, and persistence, she could build a life much bigger than her pain.
